title: Quinoa: Protein, Fiber, and Nutrition

seo.title: Quinoa: Protein, Fiber, and Nutrition
seo.meta_description: Cooked quinoa provides about 120 calories, 4.4 g protein, and 2.8 g fiber per 100 g. Dry quinoa looks much more concentrated because it contains less water.
seo.search_intent: Understand quinoa nutrition and the difference between dry and cooked values.

excerpt: Cooked quinoa provides about 120 calories, 4.4 g of protein, 21 g of carbohydrate, and 2.8 g of fiber per 100 g in USDA reference data. Dry values are much higher per 100 g because the grain has not absorbed cooking water yet.
content_html:
Quinoa is often marketed for protein, but its nutrition is broader than one number. It is a carbohydrate-rich pseudocereal with more protein and fiber than many cooked refined grains, plus minerals such as magnesium, phosphorus, and iron.

A useful reference: 100 g cooked

USDA FoodData Central lists cooked quinoa at roughly 120 calories, 4.4 g protein, 21 g carbohydrate, 1.9 g fat, and 2.8 g fiber per 100 g. A cooked cup around 185 g provides roughly 8 g protein.

That is meaningful for a grain-like side dish, but it does not match cooked lentils, which commonly provide more than 8–9 g protein per 100 g.

Why dry quinoa looks much higher in protein

Dry quinoa is around 14 g protein per 100 g because it contains far less water. Cooking adds water and increases weight, so the protein becomes distributed through a larger mass.

The amino-acid profile is a strength

Quinoa contains all essential amino acids and is relatively rich in lysine compared with many cereal grains. That describes protein quality, not an unusually high total protein content.

Fiber and minerals

At roughly 2.8 g fiber per 100 g cooked, quinoa clearly exceeds cooked white rice, which is often below 1 g per 100 g. It also contributes magnesium, phosphorus, manganese, and iron.

Quinoa is useful because it combines carbohydrate, good-quality protein, fiber, and micronutrients—not because it is a protein powder in grain form.

faq.question: How much protein is in cooked quinoa?
faq.answer: About 4.4 g per 100 g cooked; a cooked cup around 185 g provides roughly 8 g.

faq.question: Why are dry quinoa numbers so much higher?
faq.answer: Dry quinoa contains less water. Cooking adds water and dilutes nutrients per 100 g.

faq.question: Does quinoa have more fiber than white rice?
faq.answer: Yes. Cooked quinoa is around 2.8 g per 100 g, while cooked white rice is typically below 1 g per 100 g.
